heading: Putin’s Interview. Several points were made; below are the key points.
body:
Shushi refugees return plan: He mentioned the October 19-20 ceasefire proposal, which Pashinyan rejected: “I managed to convince Aliyev to end the hostilities, but the return of refugees, including to Shusha, was a mandatory condition.” Putin was surprised that the Armenian side rejected the plan and did not understand the hypothetical threat that Armenia feared, stating that Armenia would retain control over Nagorno-Karabakh including Shusha; Pashinyan told Putin that the country would not agree.
CSTO intervention: Putin repeatedly mentioned the fact that Armenia did not recognize Nagorno-Karabakh’s independence, conveying the point that CSTO intervention would be illegitimate because it was not in Armenian sovereign territory but in internationally recognized Azerbaijan’s territory. This foreshadows later CSTO discussions, when Azerbaijan attacked Armenia.
All obligations met: Putin mentioned that all the bilateral obligations that Russia had towards Armenia she had met. That includes military technical cooperation for which the prime minister expressed gratitude on numerous occasions.
Criticism of Armenia’s political situation: “A country at war cannot afford to behave in a way that splits society from within.” At first glance, it was a criticism of Pashinyan’s velvet revolution, but also around that time, the opposition movement began. It could also be referring to the installation of the “black and white” rhetoric.

heading: meeting in Sochi.
body: Pashinyan: “I want to highlight again the role you played in stopping the 44-day war and deploying Russian peacekeepers in Nagorno-Karabakh.”

heading: Russia accuses Azerbaijan of violating November 9 agreement.
CSTO Summit, first criticism from Pashinyan.
body: Pashinyan: “It is saddening the fact that Armenia’s membership in CSTO did not restrain Azerbaijan’s aggressive actions (three times in the past two years).” He mentioned that CSTO managed to take care of Kazakhstan’s internal problem overnight. He then went on: “Since May 11, 2021, Azerbaijan used armed forces three times and occupied about 140 square kilometers of the sovereign territory of the Republic of Armenia. This happened on May 11, 2021, November 14, 2021 and September 13, 2022.”

heading: Pashinyan has questions about the essence of the Russian peacekeeping operation.
body: Mentions key violations by Azerbaijan in Nagorno-Karabakh since the November ceasefire, under the watch of peacekeepers.

heading: Meeting in St. Petersburg: Lachin blockade: “...corridor is not under peacekeepers’ control․”
Pashinyan press conference.
body: Pashinyan again points to the “fact that Russia’s lack of response means that Russia’s military presence in Armenia not only does not guarantee Armenia’s security but creates threats to Armenian security.” Pashinyan also announced that CSTO will not have its military training in Armenia and reiterated the concerns that if Russia says that Armo-Azeri border is not demarcated, then we should discuss what is CSTO’s area of responsibility in Armenia.

heading: Zakharova’s press conference.
body: Official representative of the Russian MFA, Maria Zakharova, said it is difficult to evaluate the positions of the Armenian side when Yerevan's announcements about the same issue are significantly different. Citing especially the meeting of foreign ministers that was agreed but Armenia pulled back.

heading: Pashinyan talks with Putin on Lachin blockade.
MFA Press Secretary comments on RF MFA announcement.
body: Reiterated the established position that the Russian peacekeeping mission did not stop the Lachin blockade, the capture of NK civilians. As well as the previous cases of the capture of 60 soldiers, occupation of Khtsaberd and Hin Tagher, and many more.

heading: Alen Simonyan’s refusal to respond to “…some secretary.” With Zakharova’s answer the next day, that the parliament speaker “ляпнул не подумав.”
Pashinyan’s interview to POLITICO Europe.
body: Reporter asked provocative questions, but Pashinyan accused Russia only after a specific question about security and Russia’s “betrayal.” Pashinyan mentioned established facts as well as the killing of an NK resident who was doing agricultural work, which happened right next to a peacekeeper. He also noted that while the peacekeeping mission has failed, he cannot say that if the peacekeepers were not there, the situation would be any better.

heading: Peskov on ARM-US military trainings on Sep 11. “This causes concern.”
body: A similar comment was made on July 12, 2024, on the second ARM-US training series on July 15-24: “This causes nothing but regret…”

heading: Pashinyan addresses the nation on Independence Day:
body: Reiterates Peacekeeping mission failure. Mentions that the Prague (Oct 6, 2022) and Brussels (May 14, 2023) agreements had recorded the Armenian SSR borders as RA state borders. As well as the signing of the Statute of Rome (Dec 2022) has allowed us to utilize ICC for external security. We signed it when it was already obvious that CSTO and Arm-Rus strategic partnership tools are not enough to ensure security. Hence, the signing of that was purely for external security purposes and not directed against CSTO or Russia.

heading: Russia’s harsh reply to Pashinyan’s address.
body: “Russia has always been loyal to its ally obligations and never put Armenia in a position where it had to choose either with us or against us…The irresponsible approach of Pashinyan’s team has caused the understandable dissatisfaction of the Armenian society and the following protests… We’re convinced Yerevan makes a huge mistake making the country a hostage to the West and majority of Armenian population understands it.” Mentions West’s previous “colorful revolutions.”

heading: Zakharova press briefing.
body: Statements on Armenia, Armenia’s pivot to EU and NATO, Armenia’s possible exit from CSTO

heading: Armenia freezes its membership in CSTO.
Lavrov’s disappointment about Armenia deciding to worsen relationship with Russia.
Armenia stops financing CSTO.
We freezed our membership not only because of their lack of action but because CSTO membership is a threat to Armenia’s security and sovereignty. Peskov rejected the statement.
Armenia trying to enter EU.
Parliament speaker, Simonyan, blames Russia for “hybrid-war” through its agent—Kocharyan.

Zakharova said Simonyan’s statement doesn’t connect the picture as a whole: “What hybrid-war can there be if Armenia is represented here at events and there are regular contacts on the highest level?”
Lavrov in Yerevan.
body: On the question that Azerbaijan used Russian weapons against Armenia, Lavrov reminded that Armenia used Russian weapons to “capture” the seven districts on which it never had any official claim.

heading: Alleged coup attempt by Archbishop Galstanyan.
A. Mirzoyan press conference.
body: Question about Lavrov mentioning the tension between the government and the church in Armenia. Mirzoyan said Lavrov is wrong, it’s not government-church but some clergy members trying to interfere in politics. It’s better that Mr. Lavrov doesn’t the internal affairs and internal politics of the Republic of Armenia.
